scope: Independent source, emitted C and actual object review of final v5 allocator framing and isolated x86 page-table teardown. No builds or VMs run by this reviewer. Runtime records remain independently owned validation inputs.
allocator_findings: For slack==0, upstream offset clamping always yields zero. The new branch skips only old offset reads/cycling arithmetic; the prior p[-4] assertion remains before the branch. All positive-slack rotation and old-header shadow writes remain.

enframe supplies its already known slot index0..31 to set_size_at. Existing set_size callers preserve the header low5bits through the wrapper. For valid size/end ranges, all redzone writes address p+n or later, so extracting the index before those writes is equivalent.

Read exact patched meta.h/malloc.c/free.c/realloc.c from all four configured musl sources; all four meta.h hashes agree. Reproduced all24 .o/.lo malloc/free/realloc disassemblies byte-for-byte with the actual GNU cross objdump.

Verified all12 mallocng static object members byte-for-byte in their actual libc.a. Archives contain wrapper free/realloc members sharing basenames, so checks enumerate every member and require exactly one matching mallocng object.
All8 emitted static/PIC free instruction sequences are identical to v4. Existing metadata-secret, bounds, live-mask, nominal/redzone, invalidation and thread-state checks remain.

Actual x86 PIC malloc at3c4 traps nonzero p[-4],3ca/3ce branches around old-offset reads for residual<=15, and47c stamps final header once after unchanged size redzones. ARM PIC268/26c check p[-4],270/274 skip positive-slack path,324 stamps header once. Actual realloc preserves old low5bits and all validations.
kernel_findings: Read the actual isolated virtual_amd64.v, not shared main source. Only frozen v4 plus reviewed teardown is reconstructed; another session main NX changes are excluded.

Successor test is bounded at index511 and accepts every nonzero entry, including software-only flags. If absent, complete scan covers all512 entries starting at zero. An earlier entry or sparse hole cannot be mistaken for emptiness.

A surviving child proves all ancestors nonempty; early return avoids needless higher scans without freeing anything. If a child empties, its parent edge is cleared before considering that parent for reclamation.

All reclaimed parent edges are detached before unconditional invalidate and any pmm_free. Local INVLPG uses a compiler memory barrier; remote invalidation follows MFENCE and waits for acknowledgments. CPUs switched away have already flushed the map; dying maps preserve the existing no-active-CPU teardown precondition.
Four-level root is never freed. Five-level PML4 is freed only when its complete scan is empty after removing PML3, with the PML5 edge cleared before shootdown; PML5 remains owned by the page map.

Read actual generated unmap/helper C and full relocation-bearing x86 object disassembly. Successor bounds and complete512 loops lower directly with no hidden V allocations. All four physical frees follow the completed shootdown callback. Kernel_pagemap and callback/free relocations resolve to intended symbols.

Independently reconstructed full18file saved patch from recorded e29 base, verified every file against both actual build manifests and isolated sources; both full architecture builds exit0 and each248standard module snapshot matches before/after.

architecture_reference.title: Intel64 and IA32 Architectures SDM Volume3A, section4.10.4.1
architecture_reference.support: INVLPG invalidates paging-structure caches for the current PCID as well as the selected page translation. This supports invalidating once after empty ancestors are detached, including when the cleared leaf was absent.

supplement_review: Reviewed pagetable.c sparse earlier-entry/index511, sibling survival across2MiB/1GiB/512GiB boundaries, absent-page faults, fork COW and zeroed address reuse. LA57 coverage must be reported separately from optional skip on a four-level CPU. Guest runs are pending at review time.

supplement_final_review.findings: Final helper retries waitpid EINTR and checks x86 CPUID leaf7 ECX.LA57 before optional256TiB mapping; absence explicitly skips only that boundary. Allocation failure is never treated as a successful supported mapping. Same final source hash appears in actual five-level/four-level x86 and ARM exit-zero run manifests; five-level raw data exercises boundary and four-level raw data explicitly skips.
